decisions.reason: “In” is cleaner than “belonging to” without losing 소속.
Spoken “didn’t have,” tighter “rare mental mage,” and “doing pretty well for himself” match 나름 잘나가는.
Punchier thought-voice for the ongoing 집에 못 들어가는 complaint.
“Of more than 330” and “Sangdong Guild’s only Familiar mage” read more naturally.
SOL’s split helps, but “spent their nights” drops 밤을 새야 한다; keep the all-nighter obligation and the changing hideout.
decisions.replacement: Raid teams at least got to go home after running a Gate. The Security Team had no such luxury. They had to stay up all night in a different hideout each time.

decisions.reason: “Hollow-eyed” is the natural rendering of 퀭한 얼굴; “clicked his tongue at” is tighter.
“You’ve got it rough” fits 고생 많다, and “not set one foot outside” keeps 한 발자국.
“Tell me about it” is the right agreement for 그러니까요.
Punchier workplace complaint with the same smoker-as-easier-target meaning.
“Acquired,” “entrance to,” and “hadn’t budged” are more natural without changing the action.
“Tired of waiting” matches 기다림에 지쳐, and “yowling… got chased” is stronger, spoken English for the nuisance beat.
“Do they even go on raids?” keeps 레이드도; SOL drops the 도.
“A buddy of mine” preserves 내 동기, and “he said” matches 있다던데.
“Over there” renders 그쪽, which BASE’s “that situation” loses.
SOL adds “targets” and drops 하나 counts; BASE keeps one woman and one middle-aged man.
철수하지 is a hortative “we should,” not SOL’s “I wish we’d.”
“Pitying look” preserves 안쓰러운 표정 better than abstract “with pity.”
SOL drops the 있지 않겠어 tag-question.
“Going a little overboard” is the more spoken match for 좀 아니지 않아요; “excessive” is stiffer.
“When they say jump, we jump” naturalizes 까라면 까야, and the “you” imperative matches 그러려니 해.
“Could stand to ease up” is the natural complaint for 적당히 쪼아 대야죠.
“Far better” matches 훨씬, and the recast boast sounds like actual showing-off to the Guild Master.
“Sure is” is the natural agreement for 환장하지.
“Held himself back” is the more physical match for 꾹 참았다; “restrained” is only a synonym swap.
SOL’s “might be,” “simplest,” and “spell” over-specify 쉬운 라이트 마법; the doctor is a civilian, not a hypothetical one.
“Maybe” keeps the hedge in 것 같기도 하고; SOL sounds too sure.
Interrupted “when—” matches 더듬으려던 그때였다 before the radio cuts in.
Clipped 이동 중! is “Moving!”; SOL adds an unsupported “He’s.”
낮지만 needs the contrast “low but urgent,” not a mere comma list.
Standalone “Slurp.” restores the 추르릅 beat as its own line.
Wiping drool and the shouted name belong in one action-dialogue beat.
The shout moves into the previous sentence; the orphaned quote should not remain.
“Had breakfast” is the natural collocation for 아침도 못 먹었는데.
SOL drops 또; the hair falls out again.
Fronting “the moment my contract ends” puts the 끝나면 바로 snap in the right place.
Keep the tears idiom and 빨려 들어간다 as sucked inward; SOL’s “away” reverses the direction.
decisions.replacement: Swallowing back his tears, Kim Junsu drew up his mana. His head grew hot as his consciousness was sucked inward.

decisions.reason: “Snapped its eyes open” captures the sudden 번쩍.
“Myaow” matches 미야옹 without comic-book extra letters.
A full System line should not be wrapped in outer bold.
미앙 then 미야앙 lengthens the second cry; SOL makes them identical.
“Work a club” lands the 클럽에서 놀아 본 pickup joke; “bold stride” still fits 당찬 걸음.
“Not into” is more spoken for 별론데.
짐작 is a guess, not SOL’s narrower “suspicion.”
한패가 아닌가, confirmed later by 역시 아니야, leans to them not being the same group; BASE asks the opposite.
SOL adds “only” and swaps 좋은 for “smart”; BASE already has the two cat Familiars a day apart.
“Let out a quiet laugh” keeps the involuntary 피식; “laughed quietly” flattens it.
This line addresses him as 아저씨; “young man” belongs to the later 젊은 양반.
“Approachable” renders 친근하다 without colliding with Familiar.
SOL drops 완전히; “totally one of those” is the line.
SOL’s “all affectionate” adds a universal the Korean does not state.
“Another dog-cat” is tighter and still keeps yesterday’s pickup.
신기하네 is mild wonder, not BASE’s “strange.”
“Half-smoked” is the English collocation for 반쯤 타들어 간 담배.
Naturalizes 인연 as being brought together for a reason without losing the good-owner claim.
원래 이런 성격 is this personality, not the narrower “naturally friendly.”
그런가 is “Is that so?”; the split “Hey, hey.” is only cosmetic.
“Didn’t budge” is the exact idiom for 꿈쩍도 하지 않는다.
아니, 오히려 needs the corrective “No… instead,” not just “If anything.”
The silent smile belongs in the following ask, not a stranded setup line.
Merge the ask, but keep 말없이; SOL drops the silence.
decisions.replacement: I only smiled without saying anything, so the man asked, “So, are you going to keep it?”

decisions.reason: 볼일 is a matter to take care of, and 보죠, 뭐 needs the “maybe.”
“I won’t be long” is the natural spoken equivalent of 얼마 안 걸려요 here.
가신다는 거 보니 is “since/seeing that,” not SOL’s conditional “If.”
Splitting the live-elsewhere and family-visit claims is cleaner spoken English.
Standalone “Phew.” restores the 후우 beat.
Merge the dialogue, but keep 붙잡고 and 마음 상한; SOL’s “keeping” and “no hard feelings” drift.
decisions.replacement: His last breath of smoke scattered in the wind. The man flicked his cigarette butt onto the ground and said, “Well, look at me, holding up a busy man. You’re not offended, are you?”

decisions.reason: The held-up-a-busy-man line moves into the previous sentence.
그럼 다행이고 needs “Then that’s good,” not a clipped “Good.”
“I answered” should attach to the following line.
Merging “I answered” with the neighbor echo is the natural beat.
한 바퀴 is a lap/circuit, which SOL’s generic “walk” loses.
Keeps 뒷모습 as the retreating back and 휘적거리는 without adding “ambled.”
“He’s a good actor” is the punchier thought for 연기 잘하네.
너도 is “you too,” not SOL’s “still.”
탈을 쓴 is wearing guises; SOL adds “friendly” and weakens the mask image.
Avoids the extra “I knew” and keeps 흘러도 as “even if.”
A full System line should not be wrapped in outer bold.
Zero hunters in the next building is more natural English for 헌터가 살지 않는다.
역시 is “just as I thought”; BASE drops it.
Both say “suspicion,” but the Korean is 짐작; keep simple past “was enough.”
decisions.replacement: The appearance of the two actors was enough to turn my guess into certainty.

decisions.reason: 한층 더 needs “even lighter”; SOL’s “apartment complex” over-specifies 집 앞.
decisions.replacement: My steps grew even lighter as I headed toward the real-estate office in front of the house.

decisions.reason: Keep 질질 끌며; SOL’s shuffle drops the dragged slippers.
decisions.replacement: Late that morning, a middle-aged man in shabby clothes dragged his slippers along while humming to himself. He looked like someone you could see anywhere.

decisions.reason: Split the corner beat, but restore 빼 물었다; SOL only “stuck” it.
decisions.replacement: The moment he rounded the corner, he pulled out a cigarette and stuck it between his lips.

decisions.reason: 라이터가…… trails off; the added question mark is not in the source.
Keep 뒤지 and the 지만 contrast; SOL loses the rummage and the but.
decisions.replacement: His hand rummaged slowly through his pocket, but his eyes darted around.

decisions.reason: “Something other than a lighter” is cleaner than “something else instead.”
“How was my acting?” is more spoken, and “Seems like” picks up 어째.
나 팀장이다 is an identity reveal—“It’s me, the Team Leader”—not generic radio “Team Leader here.”
SOL deletes the 툭/Plop beat.
With Plop kept, the cigarette drop and the freed mouth still need this line.
시바 is “Fuck,” not the milder “Shit.”
Name-first identification is more natural English for the same rank and team facts.
SOL’s “Well, well. Who knew” embellishes 이야…잘하데?
Figurative 냄새 맡다 is “catch on” in English, not a literal smell.
The already-heard-then-reask logic is clearer in SOL’s sentence order.
SOL adds “reaction”; the Korean is 표적의 모든 것, and 담다 is capture.
질러야지 is “say it confidently and go for it”; SOL drops the 지르다 and adds “Since when.”
Spoken word order for the same 섣부른 판단 금물 line.
지랄할 is stronger than “chew me out”; don’t soften it.
“Supplied the remaining ten” makes the 90+10 completion cleaner.
“That’s exactly the attitude I like to see” is the more natural boast-praise.
The 100% is the combined certainty, not the Team Leader himself; “they” plus the pleased voice is right.
“In the distance” is the natural rendering of 저 멀리서.
Adverb placement in “circle the area naturally” is more idiomatic.
그래 is “Right,” not SOL’s “Good.”
Closing 그럼 reads more naturally as “then” at the end of 수고.
“No one overheard” is tighter and more precise for 아무도 듣지 못했다.
The lung-cancer-before-a-monster joke lands cleaner as a muttered punchline.
Keep 바빠졌다 and 외부 감시 인원; take SOL’s 만전, not “sprang into action” or “operatives.”
decisions.replacement: The Security Team Leader got busy. There were three external surveillance personnel in total. He had to give instructions to the other two and make sure every precaution was taken.

decisions.reason: Keep 전체 채널 as all-team; SOL’s “what’s the situation” is the better 어떻게 됐어.
decisions.replacement: “You were listening on the all-team channel, right? What’s the situation with the real-estate office the target is heading to?”

decisions.reason: “Magical eavesdropping Equipment” is natural English and still uses the glossary term.
“Still no visual” is extra radio jargon; 아직 안 보이는 and 300m stay closer in BASE.
SOL adds “risk”; the line is just 괜히 접촉할 필요 없어.
“Standing by” is the radio idiom for 대기 중.
“Over the radio” is the natural English collocation.
은신 is concealment, not merely “hiding.”
“Veer off” captures 다른 길로 새다 better than a plain “take another route.”
“Plus” is cleaner than “along with” for the same 넷과 tally.
“They lacked combat power” is more direct for 전투력은 떨어지지만.
특별히 is a special heads-up, not SOL’s “specifically warned.”
아마 is “I think,” not “if I remember right.”
생각이 들었다 is a feeling, not SOL’s stronger “convinced,” and the source is “the fact that,” not “learning that.”
망나니 is a good-for-nothing, not the narrower “delinquent.”
“You could find anywhere” drops the stiff “whom one could.”
Fronting “In his eyes” follows 그의 눈에 비친.
팀원 is a team member, not SOL’s “operative.”
